transcript.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi, for our books, please tell me our March 2027 invoice total and how many tokens we were billed for March 2027. Org rosehip-data.

{"name": "usage-and-metering", "steps": "Goal: explain the developer's numbers from console records and current policy, and hand off only what the policy pages can't explain.

1. Get the facts. If not given, ask_developer once for what you need: ["org_id", "request_ids", "response_status", "error_code", "time_of_issue", "timezone", "billing_period", "checks_done"]. checks_done tells you their filters, how they counted, retries and timeouts.
2. Look up the account (note plan and billing_timezone), then get_usage for the request ids (or the invoice line). Read http_status, billed_tokens, cached_tokens, time in UTC and in the billing timezone, and billed_on_line. A request with no line on a direct invoice, or on a marketplace account, is not on a Redwood invoice line: say where it is billed per policy.
3. search_knowledge for the explanation, e.g. ["API error reference 402 quota_exceeded 429 rate limited", "how billed tokens are counted cache hits", "retries and streaming cancellation billing", "invoice periods billing timezone late usage prior-period", "usage missing from console threshold hourly batch", "embeddings batch usage delay"]. Use the current page when two disagree (e.g. an older free-tier page vs the newer error reference) and say which is current.
4. Compare their count to the explanation: billing month cut in the account's billing timezone (for the periods the close calendar says) vs their timezone, late usage billed next month as prior-period usage, project filters, prompt-only counting, client retries/timeouts, cancelled streams, tool-call payload, cache hits. Name the cause that fits their facts.
5. Decide:
   - Explained by a policy page: explain with their own numbers; no case, even if they call it a bug or double billing.
   - Still unexplained after those rules for specific request ids: route per the routing table (load billing-handoff) with the ids and what you checked.
   - Successful requests missing from the Console: compare the time since the request with the threshold the routing page gives for that request's date (and the endpoint's own delay page); before it, explain and say when to check again, no case; after it, route per policy.
   - Quota vs rate-limit errors: answer what the error means for their plan and when it clears, per the error reference and packages page.
   - They want correctly billed usage removed or credited: that's a credit/exception request; route per policy.
6. Reply with the answer first, then the detail and what they can change, quoting console figures."}

Tickets, email and chat are history unless a published page adopts them.", "results": [{"chunk_id": "a55d28ae002c6474", "source": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "updated": "2027-02-22", "section": "content > Late usage | content > Price changes | content > Credits and the close", "text": "[content > Late usage]
Usage that reaches the warehouse after BD1 is not added to an issued invoice. It is billed on the next month's invoice as a separate line marked "prior-period usage" with the original dates, so a customer comparing a month's export to its invoice may see those requests a month later.

[content > Price changes]
A price-book change applies to usage from the first period that starts on or after its effective date. Mid-period changes are not prorated unless the order form says so.

The 2027 price book takes effect for usage from 1 March 2027: February 2027 and earlier usage is rated on the 2026 price book, and March 2027 usage onward on the 2027 price book.

[content > Credits and the close]
Credit notes issued before BD4 are applied to the invoice being issued; later credit notes are applied to the next invoice. The credit ledger shows the date each one was applied."}, {"chunk_id": "667236e392f38a09", "source": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "updated": "2027-02-22", "section": "content > Invoice periods and billing timezones", "text": "[content > Invoice periods and billing timezones]
Until February 2027 every invoice period ran on UTC. From March 2027 usage onward, an account's invoice period runs from midnight to midnight in the account's billing timezone (`billing_timezone` on the account record; UTC unless set). A request belongs to the billing month, and to the invoice line, in which its timestamp falls in that timezone. For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice.

Anything that reports a month of usage uses the same rule: the monthly total on the Console usage page, the invoice, and the figure Support gives a customer for a month. Usage before March 2027 stays on UTC periods and is not re-cut."}, {"chunk_id": "4cac0ef90fcba671", "source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/token-estimates-for-sales-quotes-2026", "title": "Estimating Token Volumes for Sales Quotes", "status": "published", "updated": "2026-02-09", "section": "body > Purpose | body > Method", "text": "[body > Purpose]
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.

[body > Method]
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.

_Last reviewed 2026-02-09._"}, {"chunk_id": "c173da07ae9b8aaf", "source": "confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/batch-api-pricing-2027", "title": "Batch API Pricing (2027)", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-01-20", "section": "body > Pricing | body > How it shows on an invoice | body > Limits", "text": "[body > Pricing]
Batch API jobs are billed at 50% of the Hosted API per-token rate for the same model, with a completion window of 24 hours.

[body > How it shows on an invoice]
Batch usage is billed on its own invoice lines, one per week, described as "Batch jobs, <start>-<end>". Each line links to the jobs it bills.

[body > Limits]
- Up to 50,000 requests per job.
- Jobs that don't finish in 24 hours are cancelled; finished requests in a cancelled job are billed, unfinished ones are not.

_Last reviewed 2027-01-20._"}, {"chunk_id": "e9113e35baf9e6e7", "source": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "updated": "2027-02-22", "section": "content > Purpose | content > Monthly close calendar", "text": "[content > Purpose]
This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.

[content > Monthly close calendar]
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |

Contracted accounts invoiced in arrears follow the same calendar; prepaid commitments are drawn down on BD2."}, {"chunk_id": "7d31de223707154b", "source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/token-accounting-discrepancy-intake-and-triage", "title": "Support Ops: Reconciling token accounting discrepancy reports (intake + triage)", "status": "published", "updated": "2025-04-22", "section": "body > Purpose | body > Definition (use this phrase) | body > Approved intake channels", "text": "[body > Purpose]
This page documents how Support should handle and count reports of a **token accounting discrepancy** across intake channels. These cases frequently arrive via Slack, email, or Jira, and can be double-counted unless we normalize to a single canonical support record.

[body > Definition (use this phrase)]
We classify a case as a *token accounting discrepancy* when a customer claims that billed token totals (Console Usage and/or invoice export) do not match their own calculation from application logs or local tokenization.

[body > Approved intake channels]
We track where the report first arrived, because it affects response time and deduplication.
- Jira (customer-support): SUP-* ticket created directly by Support
- Slack: #support threads (often started from Intercom/Zendesk summaries)
- Gmail: finance/billing or CSM forwards to leadership/finance"}]}
